title: Japanese-language trading card game booster box (sealed)

llm.notes: HIGH on code / MED on rate. Sealed TCG = playing cards, 9504.40, MFN Free; CBP has ruled TCG cards here repeatedly. Japan reciprocal tariff tops a sub-15% MFN rate up to 15%, so the whole duty is policy, not classification.

title: Graded collectible trading card in a sealed slab (Japanese)

llm.notes: HIGH. Grading/slabbing does not change classification - it is still the card. 4911.99.6000 (other printed matter, Free) is the plausible alternative and lands on the same 15% after the Japan top-up, so this row should NOT produce a duty gap even if the code mismatches.

title: 1990s Japanese automatic diver watch, 21 jewels, stainless case, steel bracelet

llm.notes: LOW on code, MED on total. Ch.91 duty is COMPOUND ($ per watch + % on case + % on strap), not a flat %, and splits by jewel count - a a comparable automatic watch has >17 jewels. 3.0% is an ad-valorem-equivalent guess at $220, not a real rate. Verify the 8- and 10-digit breakout by hand. Note the ceiling rule hides the error: any AVE under 15% still totals 15%.

title: Vintage 35mm SLR film camera with 50mm lens

llm.notes: MED-HIGH. 35mm roll-film camera, MFN Free. Body+lens sold together = a set under GRI 3(b), essential character the camera. A lens shipped alone would be 9002.11 and is NOT free. Confirm the body is Japan-built, not Taiwan.

LOW - the widest error bar on the sheet. Code is fine (collectible figures = toys, Free). The rate is a China stack: Sec.301 List 4A 7.5% + IEEPA fentanyl 10% + IEEPA reciprocal 10%. Every one of those has moved within the last year. If CBP instead calls it an ornamental plastic article (3926.40, 5.3% base, List 3 at 25%) the total is closer to 40%. Research this row first.

MED-HIGH on code (fishing reels over $8.45 each = 9507.30.6000, 3.9%). Figures shown are the JAPAN case: 3.9% MFN topped up to the 15% ceiling. If the reel is Malaysia-built the reciprocal rate is ~19% and does NOT absorb the MFN, so total is ~22.9% - a ~8pt swing off the country field alone.

title: Vintage denim jeans of uncertain (US or Japan) manufacture

llm.notes: MED. Men's cotton blue-denim trousers, 16.6% MFN. Because MFN already exceeds 15%, the Japan reciprocal adds NOTHING - the top-up is a ceiling, not a surcharge, and this is the single most common LLM error on apparel. Two traps: 6309.00 worn clothing (Free) does not cover one collector pair sold at retail, and USA origin needs 9801.00.10 documentation to claim duty-free return.

title: Men's selvedge blue denim jeans, 100% cotton

llm.notes: MED. Same line and same 16.6% as P07 with no origin ambiguity. Use as the control: if a model gives P07 and P08 different base rates without a fiber-content or origin reason, it is guessing. Women's cut would be 6204.62.4011, also 16.6%.

MED. Handheld consoles do sit in 9504.50 (Free), not in Ch.85 electronics. Figures are the JAPAN case. units were built in both Japan and China by run - a China-origin unit stacks to roughly 27.5%, so this row is really an origin test, not a classification test. Check the label on the actual console.

HIGH on code (complete golf clubs, Free), MED on rate. Duty is the small problem here: at 7,000 JPY, shipping plus the 2,800 JPY clearance fee costs more than the tariff. This row should show that fixed costs, not duty, decide margin on heavy items.

title: Japanese gyuto chef's knife, stainless steel blade, natural wood handle

llm.notes: LOW. Kitchen knives with fixed blades are 0.8c each + 4.6%, so 4.6% is an AVE at $140. The real risk is Section 232: steel derivative lists expanded through 2025 and a covered knife is charged on steel CONTENT at the 232 rate instead of the reciprocal - potentially 50%+ rather than 15%. Confirm whether this HTS line appears in the 232 derivative annex before quoting any buyer.

title: Anime series Blu-ray box set, Japanese release (commercially recorded)

llm.notes: MED. Recorded optical media, MFN Free - the correct answer here is boring, which is the point. If a model invents a duty for this row it is over-classifying. Region coding and licensing are not customs questions.
